key_insight: This paper argues that strong math performance in LLMs may hide a missing underlying "primitive" for true structural mathematical understanding. It introduces a way to diagnose those gaps and use the findings to improve post-training.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of determining whether LLMs truly understand mathematical structure or are mainly pattern-matching their way through problems, and how to repair weaknesses in that understanding.
method: Define and use a "Mathematical Primitive" to probe specific structural capabilities in LLMs.
Systematically diagnose which components of mathematical understanding are present or missing.
Leverage diagnostic results to guide post-training improvements for better mathematical reasoning.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more principled way to evaluate math reasoning beyond final-answer accuracy. It also offers a path to make models more reliable on complex mathematical tasks by targeting the real source of failure.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: diagnose -> identify missing primitive -> repair via post-training
Capability matrix showing present vs. missing mathematical primitives
Before/after performance chart on mathematical reasoning tasks
Icon set for structure, reasoning, diagnosis, and improvement
paper_title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper_authors: Shuo Xing, Zilin Dai, Chengyuan Qian, Fangzhou Lin, Wenjing Chen
